vulnerability.title: Werkzeug safe_join accepts leading-slash and UNC-style path components on Windows with Python < 3.11 before 3.0.6, allowing paths outside the base directory

critical_operation.code_excerpt:
if (
            any(sep in filename for sep in _os_alt_seps)
            or os.path.isabs(filename)
            or filename == ".."
            or filename.startswith("../")
        ):
            return None
critical_operation.description: safe_join() normalizes each untrusted component with posixpath.normpath and then rejects it only if it contains an OS alternate separator (backslash on Windows), os.path.isabs() is true, it is exactly "..", or it starts with "../". On Windows with Python < 3.11, ntpath.isabs() returns False for UNC paths such as //server/share, and posixpath.normpath leaves "//b/c" unchanged, so components beginning with "//" (and plain "/..." components, which os.path.isabs also misses on some Windows/Python combinations) survive the check. posixpath.join then returns a path rooted outside the base directory (or on a UNC share). The missing predicate is exactly `filename.startswith("/")`, which the 3.0.6 fix adds at lines 154-155.

entry_point.description: SharedDataMiddleware.get_directory_loader's loader passes the client-derived path to safe_join(directory, path) at line 206; __call__ obtains that path with get_path_info(environ) at line 229. If safe_join returns a "//..." value, os.path.isfile(path) / self._opener(path) at line 213 operate on that path outside the intended directory. send_from_directory (utils.py:563) is a second public caller whose `path` argument is documented as the client-provided part.

trace.description: Client request path is taken from the WSGI environ
Untrusted path is passed to safe_join(directory, path)
Predicate block lacks the leading-slash check, so "//b/c" is accepted on Windows Python < 3.11
Returned path is checked with os.path.isfile and opened, resolving outside the base directory

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA (GitHub_M) supplies the CVSS 4.0 6.3 metric and CWE-22 and points at the advisory, fix commit 2767bcb1 and release 3.0.6. NVD carries both that Secondary metric and its own Primary CVSS 3.1 5.3 assessment (Analyzed), so it adds independent analysis rather than only mirroring. OSV repeats the CNA vector, records the same commit and both the tag commit 5eaefc39 and 2767bcb1 as fixed GIT events, and adds PYSEC-2026-2045. All three published sources agree on the MEDIUM level (6.3/6.3/5.3 are all MEDIUM); the scores and CVSS versions differ, which is acceptable because the level agrees. The git evidence matches the stated fixed version: 3.0.6 is the first tag whose safe_join carries the predicate, 3.0.2-3.0.5 do not.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No code was executed: there was no Windows host and no Python < 3.11 interpreter, so the os.path.isabs/ntpath behaviour is taken from the upstream advisory and comment, not reproduced.

The flaw only manifests on Windows with Python < 3.11 and only when the application passes attacker-controlled components to safe_join (SharedDataMiddleware or send_from_directory); applications on other platforms are not affected, and an end-to-end exploit was not attempted.
NVD's Primary CVSS 3.1 5.3 differs in score from the CNA CVSS 4.0 6.3; both are MEDIUM, so severity level agrees, and the dossier records the CNA metric as primary.
The local mirror is shallow at fix merge 2767bcb1, so cross-release ancestry through it (e.g. merge-base against 3.0.5) is not reliable; the dossier relies on tag trees and blob ids instead.
The advisory gives no reporter or reproduction reference, so no independent reproduction is available and grade A is not attainable.
open_questions: Whether every Python < 3.11 Windows build misses os.path.isabs for both "//server/share" and single-slash "/x" forms was not executed; the fix's leading-slash check covers both.
Whether any 3.0.x release between 3.0.3 and 3.0.5 contains an unrelated safe_join change was checked only by blob id (identical 9999509d), not by a full release-by-release diff.
Whether applications using only safe_join for non-filesystem purposes (e.g. URL path joining) are affected was not assessed; the CVE speaks of unintended access to data.
